transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
The French government says it's preparing vast security measures
for Saturday's nationwide demonstrations.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports from Paris.
Along with tens of thousands of police,
security operations will be reinforced by Operation Sentinel,
a military contingent that patrolled French streets
and the terrorist attacks in 2015.
President Macron held a security meeting this morning
over the crisis that is casting a dark cloud
over the waning days of his presidency.
Macron and his government are being blamed
by the far left and far right
for letting the violence get out of control
and for the underlying conditions motivating the protesters.
What began in mid-September as a student protest
for improved facilities and more teachers
has ballooned into a general movement involving unions
and public sector workers against the high cost of living
and what they say are growing inequalities.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Paris.
Michigan's Senate race was the focus last night
in suburban Detroit, where the Republican incumbent
and Democratic nominee faced off in a debate.
Russ McNamara with Michigan Public Radio has more.
With low approval ratings and high gas prices,
Democratic candidate Abdul El Sayed tried to tie his opponent,
Republican Mike Rogers, to President Trump
during the debate at WXYZ-TV.
This is what you're going to get.
Donald Trump policies, it's not working for any of us.
This kind of chaos just doesn't work.
In response, Rogers says he will stand up to the president
if the policy isn't working.
It's good for Michigan, I'm going to be for it.
If it's bad for Michigan, I'm going to be against it.
President Trump will be in Michigan for a rally on Sunday.
Former President Obama will be stumping for El Sayed
in Detroit on Saturday.
For NPR News, I'm Russ McNamara in Detroit.
A new survey shows the monthly costs for health plans
through employers in the U.S. rose this year.
NPR's Selena Simmons Duffin reports
this increase was running about the same as inflation.
The nonpartisan health research organization KFF
just released its annual survey of nearly 2,000 employers
about their health benefits.
Health insurance costs have been going up fast for years,
so even though this year's increase is 5 percent,
about the same as wage growth and inflation,
all those increases add up.
On average, premiums for a family of four
now cost $28,000 per year, says Matthew Ray of KFF.
Which is just a ton of money.
It's basically the cost of a new car every year
just to keep a family of four insured.
Of that total, the survey found the share that workers pay
rose to more than $7,400 per year on average.
So even people with great health coverage through work
are putting a lot of their income towards health insurance.
Selena Simmons Duffin, NPR News.
On Wall Street, the Dow Jones Industrial Average
is down nearly 80 points.
The NASDAQ is down 300.
This is NPR.
The Trump administration says it will loan up to
315,000 barrels of heating oil to Americans this winter.
The fuel will be exclusively used in Connecticut,
Massachusetts, and Maine.
Trump will tap up to one-third of the
U.S. Emergency Heating Oil Reserve.
Up to a third of homes in New England need this heating oil.
Prices for the fuel have skyrocketed.
Public schools in Toledo, Ohio are open today
now that a shelter-in-place order has been lifted.
There was a massive chemical leak that started Tuesday night.
Still, people living within a half mile of the
chemical terminal in North Toledo
have been told to stay away.
The facility is close to the Michigan border.
The cause of the leak still isn't known.
One person has been injured.
Pope Leo's doctors say he will not need further treatment
following lung surgery to remove a cancerous growth.
Alejandra Hertzler-McKane of Religion News Service reports.
Pope Leo was back to praying with crowds in St. Peter's Square
just a week after surgery to remove the lower lobe of his right lung.
After his surgery, the pontiff was diagnosed with lung cancer.
But doctors say that tests have confirmed that the pope's cancer was localized
and he won't need more treatment.
At the Vatican, the pope thanked the faithful for supporting him with their prayers.
In just over two weeks, Leo is scheduled to undertake a grueling 12-day trip.
Fourteen flights will take him across Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru,
his former home base as a missionary and later as a bishop.
For NPR News, I'm Alejandra Hertzler-McKane.
You're listening to NPR.

topics.text: French government prepares heavy security, including military patrols, for Saturday's nationwide protests
Michigan Senate candidates Abdul El Sayed and Mike Rogers clash in suburban Detroit debate
Survey finds average annual family health premiums through employers reached about $28,000
Trump administration to loan up to 315,000 barrels of heating oil to Connecticut, Massachusetts, and Maine
Toledo public schools reopen after chemical leak shelter-in-place order is lifted
Pope Leo's doctors say no further cancer treatment needed after lung surgery
